messages:
incident-bot: PAGER: gpu-decode-oom (sev-1) detected on cluster-west-2. 27% of streaming decode nodes reporting CUDA OOM during tail generation. Auto-quarantine triggered.

sara (oncall): seeing ~200 request drops/min on the streaming tier, errors look like `cuda out of memory` in decode. Rolling back recent routing?

kevin: pushed a model-config change for a canary earlier today — might be related. It increased max_tokens to 8192 for the v2-chat route.

maya: grabbing logs now. initial grep shows long-running sessions with unbounded generation where client-side max_tokens absent. KV cache growth correlated with session duration.

eng-runtime: to confirm, kernel traces show allocation spikes around decode loop when sequence length > 4k. Fallback path not triggering because quantized variant isn't compatible with that model.

kevin: that config change added `max_tokens: 8192` globally by mistake (should've been per-experiment). Oof.

sara (oncall): immediate mitigation: can we enforce a hard cap at the ingress layer (nginx) to 2048 and disable streaming for that route?

eng-runtime: yes we can push a fast ACL rule to reject requests with >2048 requested or missing max_tokens header. Preparing patch: `curl -X POST https://ops-api/rules -d '{"route":"/v2/chat/*","max_tokens":2048}'`

maya: starting node rotation of the 6 hottest nodes (quarantine + drain) to free GPU memory and flush KV caches.

tomas (cs): flagged two enterprise customers experiencing partial request drops. Opening CS tickets, will update with timeline.

sara (oncall): applying ingress cap now. will monitor error rate and latency. :hourglass_flowing_sand: 

eng-runtime: ingress rule applied (ID r-84f3). Rejects now returning 429 + body: "request max_tokens exceeds allowed limit".

maya: quarantine + drain in progress. live telemetry: request drops down from 200/min -> 40/min after ingress cap, but some latency spikes remain on warm sessions.

kevin: reverting the global canary config right now to restore previous max_tokens default (512). Deploying rollback to config service.

sara (oncall): rolling restart of streaming workers scheduled once rollout confirms.

eng-runtime: config rollback completed — new config fetched by edge within 20s. Observability: average allocation per decode dropped ~35%.

maya: node rotation complete for initial set. few pods restarted, no container crash loops observed.

tomas (cs): notified customers about mitigation and asked for examples/trace ids for impacted requests. they want an ETA for full fix.

sara (oncall): ETA tentatively 2h for full remediation (ingress cap + config rollback + drained nodes). will update if we see regression.

kevin: root cause notes: change introduced a global max_tokens override. combined with clients that omit max_tokens led to runaway generation and KV growth -> OOM. Adding a lint in config deploys to block global max_tokens > 2048.

eng-runtime: follow-ups: (1) add safety short-circuit in decode loop to cap effective tokens by runtime policy, (2) make quantized fallback compatible for this model family, (3) add per-request KV size telemetry to detect growth earlier.

maya: creating incident-channel and starting timeline capture for postmortem. Linking logs: https://logs.internal/streams/1727605432

tomas (cs): customer update sent: "mitigation in place, config rolled back, node drains completed. monitoring shows request drops reduced by ~80%. We'll follow up with RCA and timeline."

sara (oncall): closing pager for now — error rates trending to baseline. leaving channel open for postmortem notes. :white_check_mark:
